owner_brief: Instead of paying us what's owed, the chopshop owner replied to my email with 'Screw you, Blood Poseurs'. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>he uses as a front: let's make this personal.
dispatch_brief: The Blood Roses have outsmarted us. They must know it's a set-up and have now targeted our other fronts in this area. Change of tactic: <Col: StageText>protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>from the bombers.

owner_brief: We need to wipe out all of this guy's businesses or no one will take the Roses seriously in San Paro again. Another team has planted some explosives on his electronics shop. <Col: StageText>Protect the Explosives</Col> from the bomb squad.
dispatch_brief: The Blood Roses could expose our whole undercover operation. They seem to know exactly which shops our people own. <Col: StageText>Defuse our Property</Col>.

owner_brief: The chopshop owner has called in some expert armed help. For the cost of all this, he coulda just paid us in the first place. <Col: StageText>Eliminate everyone </Col>he has hired.
dispatch_brief: Enough is enough. We need to <Col: StageText>take out </Col>this group of <Col: StageText>Blood Roses </Col> before our whole undercover operation is blown wide open.

owner_brief: The names of the jury in a pending case against the G-Kings has been leaked. Arlon Benjamin wants us to make sure they vote the right way. <Col: StageText>Plant a car bomb </Col>under the <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col> of the head juror.
dispatch_brief: A big trial against the G-Kings is about to get under way, and they have a reputation for leaning on jury members. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>of the head juror from car bomb attacks.

owner_brief: This second jury member is a gardener, apparently. <Col: StageText>Plant the bomb in his van</Col>. Geddit? Plant? I crack myself up sometimes.
dispatch_brief: A second <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>is nearby, belonging to another witness. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the vehicle from the G-King bombers.

owner_brief: The law says you should be judged by your peers, but no one is as awesome as the G-Kings. So <Col: StageText>plant the car bomb </Col>under this juror's car and he can feel the awesomeness for himself.
dispatch_brief: If you don't stop these car bombs, the G-Kings on trial will be aquitted. This <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>, belonging to a jury member,  will probably be the next target. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>it.

owner_brief: Who lives in San Paro and doesn't own wheels? This loser juror, apparently - but the G-Kings are equal opportunity bombers. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>her <Col: StageText>shop </Col>and we'll have one more vote of 'not guilty'.
dispatch_brief: The G-Kings have changed tactic and targeted the workplace of a jury member. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>shop </Col>from the bombers. We must give every citizen the confidence to stand up against thugs.

owner_brief: One of the jury members dropped out; you intimidated well, my friend. We've planted a bomb at the store of his replacement. <Col: StageText>Protect the bomb</Col> from the authorities.
dispatch_brief: Well done; the big trial is going ahead as planned. But the G-Kings have changed tactic to focus on the star witness instead. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that has been set at his place of work.

owner_brief: Your campaign of friendly influencing has drawn attention - big time. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>the incoming <Col: StageText>opposition</Col> - or the jury will feel free to vote anyway they see fit. Can't have that.
dispatch_brief: The G-Kings are set on intimidating everyone involved in this trial. San Paro must have faith in its Enforcers. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>and defeat any <Col: StageText>G-Kings </Col>involved in perverting the course of justice.

owner_brief: A city street-cleaner removed all our graffiti from the nearby block. Other gangs may try to take this territory. <Col: StageText>Spray </Col>our tags back onto the <Col: StageText>walls </Col>and keep it G-King.
dispatch_brief: The graffiti removal team has been in and cleaned off all the G-King filth. But the Gs are stubborn and stupid enough to come back to reapply their tags. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>from being sprayed.

owner_brief: Are you on a sightseeing trip or something? Pick up the pace. Get over to our territory and <Col: StageText>tag these two spots, </Col>before some local bad boys take a shine to it. Don't let anyone try and mess with your work.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the G-Kings from respraying their tags on to these two <Col: StageText>locations</Col>. I don't go around putting graffiti on *their* stuff. Well... one time I did.

owner_brief: It's starting to look a bit more G around here again. Broken-in, like wearing your favorite leather knife sheath. <Col: StageText>Spray </Col>these last couple of <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and don't let anyone beat you to it.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the last couple of <Col: StageText>locations </Col>from the G-King graffiti crew who want to claim this area.

owner_brief: Job done - now muzzle your nozzle and <Col: StageText>lock and load</Col>. A graffiti removal team is headed your way - <Col: StageText>take them out</Col>.
dispatch_brief: Washing off graffiti isn't the answer: it just comes back. We need to wash the G-King scum themselves into the sewer. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>G-King taggers</Col>.

owner_brief: The Tigers have been an annoyance lately, interfering with our contracts. We need to slow them down, and luckily we've got a plan. Start by <Col: StageText>raiding </Col>these minor dealers' <Col: StageText>drug dens</Col>.
dispatch_brief: The Blood Roses seem to be 'rehearsing' for Hell Night; we've had reports of Blood Rose crime all over San Paro. <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>Blood Rose <Col: StageText>raids </Col>on these local <Col: StageText>properties</Col>.

owner_brief: Excellent. Those drugs are going to appear in Orlenz's possession soon. For that trick to happen, you need to <Col: StageText>steal </Col>his <Col: StageText>car</Col>. He's visiting Tigers in the area, so it should be easy to find.
dispatch_brief: Jeung usually only lets his Roses off the leash once a year, but he must be feeling generous today. Lucky us. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>from Blood Roses out to steal it.

owner_brief: Good, good. Now <Col: StageText>deliver </Col>the car and <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>to the stage we've set. Will this setup get that smarmy asshole Orlenz' convicted? I doubt it, but it'll cause the Tigers some trauma at least.
dispatch_brief: The Blood Rose revelers are escaping with <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them. These Hell Night events can rival the CSA riots for mass looting. Thank heck this isn't the actual Hell Night...

owner_brief: An "anonymous tip" would make them suspect the Blood Roses straight away. <Col: StageText>Hack </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna, </Col>and we'll use the Tiger radio network to send false reports guiding them to the drugs instead.
dispatch_brief: The Roses have worked themselves up into a frenzy with all the other crimes they've committed, and now they're targeting our property as well. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>from the Blood Rose revelers.

owner_brief: Our play is set, but you've left a loose end. Some people spotted you with the car. You need to <Col: StageText>kill the witnesses, </Col>or our little plan won't work. You do want the plan to work... don't you?
dispatch_brief: Trying to stop these Hell Night 'rehearsal' crimes is getting us nowhere. Time to treat the disease rather than the symptoms: <Col: StageText>take out </Col>the <Col: StageText>Blood Roses</Col>. They can't cause trouble if they're dead.

owner_brief: Some of my compañeros got hooked on Fade, and now they just sit around spaced out and doing fuck-all. It's boring, so I want to help them kick the habit. <Col: StageText>Raid </Col>their <Col: StageText>houses </Col>and steal the Fade.
dispatch_brief: A rookie of ours made the mistake of trying to hit on Double-B. We're still finding pieces of him. His unit retaliated, and now we've got a war on our hands. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the G's <Col: StageText>attacks </Col>on our <Col: StageText>homes</Col>.

owner_brief: I know Monkeywrench hides Fade in his ride. He's out cold at the moment, so just <Col: StageText>steal </Col>his <Col: StageText>car </Col>for now. I'll get it back to him later, so don't fuck the car up too much - or you're paying for it.
dispatch_brief: This little war that's broken out between us and the G-Kings is worse than usual. Getting too close to home for me, even. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>my <Col: StageText>car</Col>: those bastards are eyeing it.

owner_brief: Cool. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the car and <Col: StageText>drugs </Col>over here. I'll get our Gs to clean the car out and dump the Fade. Sucks to do this, but those asshole friends of mine will thank me for it later.
dispatch_brief: The G-Kings are a pain to deal with at the best of times; if only that rookie hadn't stirred up the hive. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>G-King looters from bringing the <Col: StageText>loot and my car </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

owner_brief: I want to make sure my compañeros don't get heat for this - <Col: StageText>hack </Col>this <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>so I can check Enforcer chatter and make sure it's all cool. If they don't ID Monkeywrench's car then we're good.
dispatch_brief: They've gotten away with people's goods, and my car - and now they're screwing with our equipment! <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>our <Col: StageText>antenna </Col>from those G-Kings.

owner_brief: Fuck! There's Praetorians on their way. Did you get spotted with the car? <Col: StageText>Kill the Enforcers </Col>so they can't interfere. I'll have to hook Monkeywrench up with new license plates now.
dispatch_brief: Ok, enough is enough. <Col: StageText>Take out </Col>the <Col: StageText>G-Kings</Col>. They really need to emphasize those 'do not fraternize with the enemy' lessons in our training. Anything to avoid another G-King incident like this.

owner_brief: A local loser is going to testify against us in court. He saw us trying to attach a tug to the Mist restaurant and tow it down the canal. <Col: StageText>Torch </Col>his <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>to make him change his story.
dispatch_brief: The Mist floating restaurant called us in to provide protection. A gang got busted trying to tow it down the canal with a tug boat and are now intimating witnesses. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this witness's <Col: StageText>vehicle</Col>.

owner_brief: I guess people don't like it when you try to tow away the floating restaurant they're eating in. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>the customers' <Col: StageText>cars </Col>to help them 'forget' the whole thing ever happened.
dispatch_brief: Who would be dumb enough to try to steal a whole floating restaurant - with people in it? These maniacs need to face their day in court. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>of the witnesses.

owner_brief: It would have been so cool to have our own floating restaurant. Shame they moored it so tightly. <Col: StageText>Burn </Col>these <Col: StageText>properties </Col>belonging to the owner and she may drop the charges against us.
dispatch_brief: This gang would be dangerous if they weren't so dumb. <Col: StageText>Protect these buildings </Col>that belong to the Mist restaurant's owner. The gang don't want her to testify in court against them.

owner_brief: The Mist restaurant has called in some bounty hunters. Looks like they want to see us either in court - or dead. <Col: StageText>Kill </Col>the <Col: StageText>bounty hunters </Col>and try to <Col: StageText>stay alive</Col>. They'll get bored eventually.
dispatch_brief: This gang are a cucumber short of a salad, you know what I mean? <Col: StageText>Eliminate the gang</Col>. You'll be doing us all a favor by removing them from the gene pool.

owner_brief: An unknown group did a series of drive-bys on our friends. <Col: StageText>Bomb </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>they used. This doesn't seem to be the work of the usual local gangs.
dispatch_brief: I love watching San Paro's Big Talent. Now the contestants who got voted off are on the hunt for revenge. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>of the show's winner from being bombed by this gang of losers.

owner_brief: The second vehicle used in the drive-by against our fellow members is nearby. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>the <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and get some payback. I'll look into who these drive-by dickwads are.
dispatch_brief: A second car is nearby, belonging to one of the Big Talent TV show judges. <Col: StageText>Protect the car </Col>from the 'The Bombastics'. If they wanted to do even more damage they'd sing instead.

owner_brief: These drive-by nuts are planning an even bigger attack. They have started to weld gun mounts onto the inside of a car. <Col: StageText>Bomb the vehicle </Col>so it can never be used against us.
dispatch_brief: These losers have a lot of anger, maybe if they'd put this much energy into their band they wouldn't have been voted off San Paro's Big Talent. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the TV exec's <Col: StageText>car </Col>from their bombs.

owner_brief: These drive-by dickwads are legitimate businessmen just killing for kicks. <Col: StageText>Blow up </Col>their <Col: StageText>store </Col>and see how they like it when we come and mess with their business.
dispatch_brief: These tuneless wonders have upped their game, unlike their talent. Now they're targeting the sponsors of the Big Talent show as revenge for being booted off. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>stores</Col>.

owner_brief: These guys don't even need the money! <Col: StageText>Protect the bomb</Col> we've planted at the other store that belongs to these part-time gangsters. They bring a whole new meaning to the term 'white collar crime'.
dispatch_brief: This group of talentless singers really hold a grudge. They are attacking the sponsor of their main rival. <Col: StageText>Defuse the bomb</Col> that's been placed at the sponsor's property.

owner_brief: Looks like these 'hobby hoods' fancy a real fight. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>off the part-time <Col: StageText>gangsters </Col>and humiliate them into never messing with real Criminals again.
dispatch_brief: We can't let these bunch of talentless singers go around causing wanton destruction. If they want to sing - it should be like a jailbird. <Col: StageText>Fight </Col>and defeat the <Col: StageText>group</Col>.

owner_brief: You know how Al Capone eventually got caught, income tax evasion. We could eliminate other gangs in the same way, by bombing their accounts. <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building</Col>.
dispatch_brief: A small, specialist gang of bombers has arrived in the area. This could be bad news. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>this <Col: StageText>building </Col>from any attempt to break in, it contains bomb casings.

owner_brief: <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>more bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building</Col>. We need it to be extra incendiary to make sure the accounting paperwork catches fire.
dispatch_brief: These bombers mean business, they plan to steal some ultra high density ballistics. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>the <Col: StageText>building </Col>where it's kept.

owner_brief: <Col: StageText>Steal </Col>the specialist <Col: StageText>bomb fuse </Col>from this <Col: StageText>building </Col>and we'll have everything we need to destroy the other gang's accounts. Who says accounting is boring?
dispatch_brief: The bomb makers are hitting another <Col: StageText>building </Col>- get there and <Col: StageText>defend </Col>it. It contains the fuses they'd need. No news on the bomb target yet.

owner_brief: <Col: StageText>Take </Col>all of the bomb <Col: StageText>components </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>so they can be assembled. I wonder if we can claim them on expenses - they are work related.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Prevent </Col>the bombers <Col: StageText>taking </Col>their <Col: StageText>components </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. They have everything they need to build some serious ordinance.

owner_brief: Head to the <Col: StageText>building </Col>where some of the gang store their accounts and plant the <Col: StageText>bomb </Col>to blow it up.
dispatch_brief: The bombers are on their way to blow up our bomb squad offices. The squad itself has been called out on a job so you'll have to <Col: StageText>defend the building </Col>from attack.

owner_brief: The other gang know we've hit them hard and they don't like it. <Col: StageText>Wipe out </Col>any <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>who remain in the area and we can take their territory. I'm sure Al Capone would approve.
dispatch_brief: With our bomb squad temporarily out of action the bombers will be a powerful force in the area. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>bombers </Col>and halt their reign of terror before it starts.

owner_brief: An economic downturn means our revenue is dropping. We had to slash the prices of all our goods and now we need more. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and grab some new stock.
dispatch_brief: The economic downturn has made the Criminals ever more desperate, they need to steal even more goods to sell. <Col: StageText>Defend these properties </Col>from being burgled.

owner_brief: WTF? Mink driving gloves? Okay, no biggie. We'll still shift 'em. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>to our <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>those stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>before they reach the burglars' <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Times are tough for everyone out there - why should the gangs get a free ride?

owner_brief: It turns out that the customers who would normally buy those mink driving gloves are staying home right now. <Col: StageText>Break into this <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and steal something for home entertaining.
dispatch_brief: More civilian properties are under attack from local burglars. <Col: StageText>Defend this building </Col>from them, the Criminals seem to be picking out only high value items.

owner_brief: Okay, I didn't actually mean a box of gold plated sex toys, but whatever. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>goods </Col>to our specialist <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>location.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Intercept </Col>the <Col: StageText>goods </Col>before those burglars get them to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. They must be planning something big with all the profit from this job.

owner_brief: A snitch has informed us of a rare guitar that's been spotted across town. <Col:StageText>Capture the item</Col> before the enforcers do, it should be worth a lot.
dispatch_brief: The burglars are planning on stealing a rare guitar. Get to it first and <Col:StageText>retreive the instrument</Col> to keep it out of criminal hands.

owner_brief: Art's also a commodity and a piece has turned up nearby. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>this second <Col: StageText>item</Col> and <Col: StageText>claim it</Col>. I've been told it's an original 'Shift' print.
dispatch_brief: There's a piece of art nearby that the burglars are targeting. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>the painting and <Col: StageText>claim it</Col>.

owner_brief: High-End Electronics sell for a fuck-ton. <Col: StageText>Get to </Col>this third <Col: StageText>item </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim it </Col>before your opponents do.
dispatch_brief: They're going for electronics now. <Col: StageText>Race </Col>the burglars to the <Col: StageText>gear </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim it </Col>for the people of San Paro.

owner_brief: There's a back-alley hospital that have foolishly left some organs unguarded. <Col: StageText>Race to </Col>the penultimate <Col: StageText>items</Col> and grab them before anyone else does. They'll sell for a fortune.
dispatch_brief: Shit, they've found an organ donor facility. <Col: StageText>Race </Col>to this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and <Col: StageText>claim the organs</Col>.

owner_brief: Screw this legal shit, there's a stash of drugs at the next place. <Col: StageText>Get to </Col>the <Col: StageText>drugs</Col> and <Col: StageText>claim them </Col>too.
dispatch_brief: Last one: The criminals have found a stash of narcotics that were hidden by a rival gang. Get there before them and <Col: StageText>grab</Col> the drugs before the crims get their hands on them.

owner_brief: Ok, collect the items and <Col:StageText>drop off the majority</Col> at our shop to sell.  We should make a lot of money off this lot.
dispatch_brief: Ok, now <Col:StageText>grab the items</Col> and <Col>drop them off</Col> at our facility. You'll need at least 3 of them.

owner_brief: We've offered a generous protection deal to the locals, but not everyone has seen sense. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and take a few things - just to highlight the value of our proposition.
dispatch_brief: We've been asked to help protect this neighborhood. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings</Col>. They're getting broken into on a regular basis.

owner_brief: That's good, hopefully they'll see the value of our insurance policies. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>loot </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. May as well sell it and get some cash.
dispatch_brief: Burglars stole cash from several buildings that fall under our jurisdiction. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the <Col: StageText>stolen property </Col>from ever <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the Criminals' <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.

owner_brief: Two local businesses have consistently ignored our messages - so we need a bigger, more personal, persuasive gesture. <Col: StageText>Burgle </Col>their <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and steal any cash or stock that you can carry.
dispatch_brief: Those burglars are getting cocky, hitting the businesses of a couple of our major clients. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>these <Col: StageText>buildings </Col>and ensure that nothing is stolen.

owner_brief: Nicely done. The business owners probably expected the Enforcers to protect them, but this is our city, not theirs. <Col: StageText>Deliver </Col>the <Col: StageText>stock </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>.
dispatch_brief: The burglars managed to grab two large <Col: StageText>bags </Col>of cash and stock from those businesses. If you can <Col: StageText>stop </Col>them <Col: StageText>reaching </Col>the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>we can save face with our client.

owner_brief: Our protection racket has proven lucrative and now everyone wants in on the action. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>to hold onto this neighborhood. Protect the protection racket.
dispatch_brief: The burglars have threatened our income and our reputation. <Col: StageText>Capture </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and prove that the Enforcers won't tolerate criminal behavior.

owner_brief: The Enforcers have been planning to hold a local fun day to draw in new recruits and win over the brain-dead citizens. Use <Col: StageText>graffiti </Col>to mark up this <Col: StageText>location </Col>and remind where the local power lies.
dispatch_brief: We have a community open day planned for this area. As usual, the gangs want to spoil it. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>this <Col: StageText>location </Col>from the gang's graffiti artists.

owner_brief: <Col: StageText>Tag </Col>some more <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them; make sure that the locals know who's in charge around here. Clue; it ain't the 'Forcers.
dispatch_brief: Graffiti artists are also targeting these <Col: StageText>locations</Col>. <Col: StageText>Defend </Col>those locations and keep this neighborhood clean and safe for our forthcoming community open day.

owner_brief: Let the Enforcers have their stupid cutesy family fun day, just so long as our graffiti looms over it. <Col: StageText>Tag </Col>these <Col: StageText>locations </Col>and then <Col: StageText>hold </Col>them.
dispatch_brief: The local gangs are keen to make their presence known during our community open day. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>these last <Col: StageText>locations </Col>from their ugly graffiti. Let's keep things clean.

owner_brief: You done the tagging, now comes the fragging. You've not be invited to the family fun day it seems. <Col: StageText>Take out </Col>these disrespectful <Col: StageText>opponents </Col>and make it clear that you don't need an invite.
dispatch_brief: You just know the gangs are going to ruin our community event if they get a chance. <Col: StageText>Eliminate </Col>the <Col: StageText>gang </Col>members, or the mofos will be back to burn down the coconut shy.

owner_brief: Our fence, Wes, is in the market for the Onset CDX-G1: an expensive media center car stereo with all the bells and whistles. Head to this <Col: StageText>vehicle </Col>and <Col: StageText>loot </Col>it: we're pretty sure it's got one.
dispatch_brief: The new multimedia car stereo from Onset is on sale today. It's already sold out, so everyone's after them. Our spotters saw thieves casing a nearby vehicle for the stereo. <Col: StageText>Protect </Col>the <Col: StageText>car</Col>.

owner_brief: Take the stolen Onset <Col: StageText> car stereo </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>point for Wes to collect. Those things cost a fortune, and they're rare as hell. Should net us a pretty penny.
dispatch_brief: Thieves took an Onset CDX-G1! <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>them taking the stolen <Col: StageText>stereo </Col>to their <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. People go crazy for anything these days... I once saw a woman stab someone over the last Kiki doll in the store.

owner_brief: A couple of our spotters hit the streets and found some more Onset stereos. <Col: StageText>Loot </Col>these <Col: StageText>vehicles </Col>and get those Onset CDX-G1s - Wes is offering us a good price for them.
dispatch_brief: A patrol identified two more vehicles being cased by thieves. <Col: StageText>Guard </Col>the <Col: StageText>cars </Col>. Those thieves're trying to make a quick buck off desperate consumers willing to buy stolen Onset stereos.

owner_brief: Nice, a couple more Onset stereos - take the <Col: StageText>stereos </Col>to the <Col: StageText>drop-off </Col>. Y'know Wes is our fence, but did you know his name is actually Wesley D. Fence? Talk about being born to do a job.
dispatch_brief: The thieves got what they were after. <Col: StageText>Stop </Col>the stolen <Col: StageText>stereos </Col>reaching the <Col: StageText>drop-off</Col>. Some cities have to deal with riots over hunger or human rights... In San Paro? Car stereos. Seriously.

owner_brief: Wes left our <Col: StageText>payment here</Col>. <Col: StageText>Recover</Col> it and <Col: StageText>keep it</Col> away from our enemies.
dispatch_brief: We need to recover those stolen Onset stereos. Some are hidden nearby: <Col: StageText>take </Col>and then <Col: StageText>keep </Col>the <Col: StageText>bag </Col>containing the stereos away from the thieves, and any crazed consumers.

owner_brief: You heard of the Goody Gundrops? Yeah? Well, we've got collectors willing to pay for the latest Gundrops figurines. We spotted people buying some from a shop: <Col: StageText>loot </Col>their <Col: StageText>cars </Col>for the models.

owner_brief: Sweet! Look at all that paint. Bet they don't want to see the Roses ruling this area. <Col: StageText>Spray</Col> one more <Col: StageText>wall</Col> for good measure.
dispatch_brief: <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> those Blood Rose vandals. Take a gun and explain, in real small, bullet-sized words, that we don't consider <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> to be an art form.

owner_brief: Stupid 'Forcers fell for it, and you can easily take out those few losers. <Col: StageText>Capture this area</Col>. Send a message that this is Blood Rose turf.
dispatch_brief: It's an ambush! <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col> and take out these wannabe paint jockeys.

owner_brief: The 'Forcers sneak around this neighborhood like a bunch of schoolgirls playing hookey. Draw them out into the open by <Col: StageText>spraying</Col> some <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col>.
dispatch_brief: Got a street patrol saying those skater-punk G-Kings are spraying <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> all over our fair city. <Col: StageText>Prevent</Col> this vandalism.

owner_brief: They ain't gonna like the the G-Kings being so bold! <Col: StageText>Spray</Col> one more <Col: StageText>wall</Col> for good measure.
dispatch_brief: The G-Kings are like tomcats pissing around to mark their territory. <Col: StageText>Stop</Col> them spraying their stinking <Col: StageText>graffiti</Col> on the walls.

owner_brief: Dumb Enforcers fell for it. <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col>and show no mercy. See how they like going toe to toe with the G-Kings!
dispatch_brief: Looks like they want to fight. Rub their noses in it! <Col: StageText>Capture the area</Col>.
